title: Out of the Stall
hook: Nose in. The way out is behind you.
scene: You parked pointed at a building you're not going into, which means leaving is a backing job — slow, one motion, into an aisle you can't see any of from where you're sitting.
decision: How do you get out of the stall?

options.text: Back out on the side mirror
options.result: The mirror gives you a slice of it. The corner of your own bumper isn't in that slice, and neither is the post you find.

options.text: Turn and look over your shoulder — slow, one motion
options.result: You twist in the seat, past the empty place beside you, and look at the actual aisle. The car comes out where you were looking.

options.text: Pull forward and cut across the stall line
options.result: You try to leave the way you're already pointed, end up across two stalls at an angle, and you're still not in the aisle.

options.text: Back out fast so it's over
options.result: You make it short by making it quick, and the aisle arrives before your look does.

debrief: Back up slowly, in one motion, looking over your shoulder at the aisle itself.

source.teaching_target: Back out of the stall by looking over the shoulder, slow, one motion. The mirror is not the look.

image_brief.camera_pose: Camera is outside the open driver door at standing height, looking in at Ali in the driver seat as she twists to look over her right shoulder toward the rear — not a passenger-seat camera, not a mirror shot.
image_brief.subject: Ali Okonjo in the driver seat of the Menace, braid over the left shoulder, wire-rim glasses, twisted right looking over her right shoulder toward the rear aisle

image_brief.midground: Ali's shoulders and the back of her head as she looks rearward; empty passenger seat with Gracie a small orange shape if visible; rear mesh beyond
